# @kesha-antonov/react-native-chat

> Chat UI for React Native, Expo and Web. A maintained continuation of
> `react-native-gifted-chat` with the same `IMessage` model and prop names. `<Chat messages
> onSend user />` alone gives a Telegram-style messenger: long-press menu, reactions, reply,
> emoji keyboard, attachment menu, voice and round video notes, photo viewer, multi-select,
> streaming (AI) replies, dark mode and theming. Also ships `ChatList`. TypeScript-first; no
> native code of its own. Compiled with the React Compiler.

This file is a condensed integration guide for AI agents. Full docs: [README](https://github.com/kesha-antonov/react-native-chat#readme).

## Install

Required peers - all four must be installed and configured:

```bash
npx expo install @kesha-antonov/react-native-chat react-native-reanimated react-native-gesture-handler react-native-safe-area-context react-native-keyboard-controller
```

Bare React Native: use `yarn add` / `npm install --save` with the same list (plus
`react-native-worklets` on Reanimated 4), then `npx pod-install`, then add Reanimated's Babel plugin
to `babel.config.js` (`plugins: ['react-native-worklets/plugin']` for Reanimated 4,
`'react-native-reanimated/plugin'` for 3), then rebuild the native app and restart Metro with `--reset-cache`.

"Cannot read property 'Chat' of undefined" at the import means a dependency threw while loading -
read the first error in the log; it is usually a native peer installed without rebuilding the app,
or (in Expo) installed with `npm install` instead of `npx expo install`.

Requires React Native >= 0.82, React 19, `react-native-gesture-handler` >= 3, iOS >= 15.1, Android API 24+,
Expo SDK 55+ (the example app runs SDK 58 / React Native 0.88).

## Minimal working example

```tsx
import { useCallback, useState } from 'react'
import { Chat, IMessage } from '@kesha-antonov/react-native-chat'

export function ChatScreen () {
  const [messages, setMessages] = useState<IMessage[]>([
    {
      _id: 1,
      text: 'Hello developer',
      createdAt: new Date(),
      user: { _id: 2, name: 'John Doe' },
    },
  ])

  const onSend = useCallback((newMessages: IMessage[] = []) => {
    setMessages(previous => Chat.append(previous, newMessages))
  }, [])

  return <Chat messages={messages} onSend={onSend} user={{ _id: 1 }} />
}
```

`Chat` fills its parent, so give it a `flex: 1` container. It mounts its own
`GestureHandlerRootView` and `KeyboardProvider` unless the app already provides them.

## Data model

```ts
interface IMessage {
  _id: string | number
  text: string
  createdAt: Date | number
  user: { _id: string | number, name?: string, avatar?: string | number | (() => React.ReactNode) }
  image?: string            // tap opens the viewer, which pages through every photo in the chat
  video?: string
  videoNote?: boolean       // with `video`: a round video note
  audio?: string            // voice note
  duration?: number         // seconds, for voice / round notes
  waveform?: number[]       // server waveform for a voice note (0..1 or 0..31)
  isMediaUnread?: boolean   // unplayed dot on a voice / round note
  isViewOnce?: boolean
  transcription?: string
  transfer?: { type: 'upload' | 'download', progress?: number, totalBytes?: number } // progress ring + cancel
  isDownloadRequired?: boolean // download arrow (`mediaTransfer.onDownload`)
  system?: boolean          // renders as a centered system notice
  isPinned?: boolean
  sent?: boolean            // ✓
  received?: boolean        // ✓✓
  pending?: boolean         // 🕓
  isFailed?: boolean        // red error badge
  editedAt?: Date | number  // "edited 14:05" (or isEdited: true)
  streaming?: boolean       // shows a typing caret while tokens arrive
  quickReplies?: { type: 'radio' | 'checkbox', values: { title: string, value: string }[], keepIt?: boolean }
  replyMessage?: { _id: string | number, text: string, user: User, image?: string, audio?: string }
  reactions?: { emoji: string, userIds: (string | number)[] }[]
  location?: { latitude: number, longitude: number }
  file?: { uri: string, name: string, size?: number, mimeType?: string } // document bubble
  linkPreview?: { url?, siteName?, title?, description?, image?, … } | null
}
```

Messages are newest-first by default (`isInverted` defaults to `true`). `Chat.append(previous, newMessages)`
prepends correctly for that ordering. The list itself (Legend List) renders oldest first, so list
indexes count from the oldest message; scroll to a message with `scrollToKey({ key: String(_id) })`.

Status is app-owned: send a message with `pending: true`, then set `sent`, then `received` as your
backend confirms. Voice notes, files and media show the same clock / ✓ / ✓✓.

## Props you will reach for first

- `messages`, `user`, `onSend` - required
- `text` + `textInputProps.onChangeText` - only if you control the composer text externally (the built-in emoji keyboard inserts either way)
- `initialText` + `onDraftChange` - restore and save the unsent draft per chat
- `theme` / `darkTheme` - deep-merged token overrides (`colors`, `radii`, `spacing`, `typography`, `bubble`, `wallpaper`, `nameColors`, …). The default look is a modern messenger style: swirl wallpaper, tails, the time on the last line; `wallpaper: { isEnabled: false }`, `bubble: { hasTail: false, isTimeInline: false }` turn those off
- `renderWallpaper` - replace the background (`null` = plain `colors.background`)
- `colorScheme` - `'light' | 'dark'` to force a scheme; omit to follow the system
- `locale` + `labels` - 15 built-in translations (es, fr, de, ru, zh, ar, pt, ja, ko, it, tr, hi, nl, pl, id; English is the default, `pt-BR` falls back to `pt`) and per-string overrides
- `renderBubble`, `renderMessageText`, `renderAvatar`, `renderInputToolbar`, … - override any component
- `isTyping` - typing indicator
- `loadEarlierMessagesProps` - `{ isAvailable, onPress, isLoading, isInfiniteScrollEnabled }`
- `isScrollToBottomEnabled` (default on, with an unread badge), `listProps` (props for the underlying [Legend List](https://legendapp.com/open-source/list/), which renders oldest first)
- `onEditMessage`, `onDeleteMessage`, `onForwardMessage`, `onPinMessage` - add Edit / Delete / Forward / Pin to the long-press menu
- `isGroupChat` (auto), `isAvatarVisible`, `isUsernameVisible` - avatars and names show in group chats only by default
- `firstUnreadMessageId` - opens on an "Unread Messages" bar
- `isLoading` - a spinner over an empty chat while history loads
- `mediaTransfer={{ onCancel, onDownload }}` - handlers for `transfer` / `isDownloadRequired`

## On by default

- Long-press menu: Reply, Copy (needs `expo-clipboard` or `@react-native-clipboard/clipboard`), then
  Forward / Pin / Edit / Delete when their callbacks are passed. Extend with
  `messageActions={(message, defaults) => [...defaults, mine]}`; `defaultMessageActions={false}` turns them off.
- Swipe left to reply (`reply={{ swipe: { isEnabled: false } }}` to turn off); tapping a quote jumps
  to the original and highlights it.
- Scroll-to-bottom button with an unread badge.
- Emoji keyboard behind the composer's emoji button (tabs, search, recents, skin tones), in the
  system keyboard's place. `emojiKeyboard={false}` hides it; `emojiKeyboard={{ columns, categories,
  recents, isSearchEnabled, renderEmojiKeyboard }}` configures it; `onPressEmoji` replaces it.
- Attachment menu behind the paperclip: photo grid with numbered picks + caption (`expo-media-library`),
  system photo picker / camera (`expo-image-picker`), File (`expo-document-picker`), Location
  (`expo-location`) - each tab only when its peer is installed. Picks arrive in `onSend` as `image`,
  `video`, `file` or `location` messages. `attachments={{ tabs, pickers, isGalleryGridEnabled, onPick, renderAttachmentMenu }}`
  configures it (`onPick` can upload first and return the messages to send); `attachments={false}`
  hides it; `actions` / `onPressActionButton` / `renderActions` replace it. iOS needs the usage strings
  (`NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription`, `NSCameraUsageDescription`, `NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription`);
  in Expo, list the packages' config plugins.
- The reactions bar's chevron opens the built-in emoji grid (`reactions.renderExpandedPicker: null` drops it).
- `getChatCapabilities()` tells which optional features the installed peers allow.

## Optional features and the peers they need

Each is inert until you install its peer; most then turn on by themselves, and every one can be turned off.

| Feature | Enable with | Extra peer dependency |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Inline video playback | `IMessage.video` | `expo-video` |
| Inline audio playback | `IMessage.audio` | `expo-audio` |
| Voice notes (hold to record) | on once the peer is installed; `audioRecording={false}` turns off | `expo-audio`, plus `react-native-audio-api` for the waveform |
| Video messages (camera notes) | on once vision-camera is installed; `videoRecording={false}` turns off, `{ isEnabled: true }` adds the system-camera fallback | `react-native-vision-camera` 5+ (with `react-native-nitro-modules` + `react-native-nitro-image`), or `expo-image-picker` |
| Note speed / auto-play / unread | `mediaPlayback={{ playbackRate, onPlaybackRateChange, onMediaRead }}`, `IMessage.isMediaUnread` (auto-play next and the "now playing" bar are on by default, `isNowPlayingBarEnabled: false` hides the bar; silent round-note loops are opt-in with `isRoundVideoAutoplayEnabled: true`) | none |
| Recording haptics | install `expo-haptics` | `expo-haptics` |
| Resume / trim a paused voice take | on with `audioRecording` | `react-native-audio-api` to resume, plus `expo-file-system` to trim (a trimmed take is sent as WAV) |
| Location messages | `IMessage.location` | none |
| Link previews | `IMessage.linkPreview`, or `fetchLinkPreview(url)` | none |
| Unread bar | `firstUnreadMessageId` | none |
| Multi-select | "Select" in the long-press menu; `onSelectionChange`, `onDeleteMessage(s)`, `onForwardMessage(s)` | `expo-clipboard` for Copy |
| Emoji reactions | `reactions={{ onReactionPress }}` (+ `Chat.toggleReaction`) | none |
| Long-press action menu | on by default; `messageActions` to extend or replace | `expo-clipboard` for Copy |
| Emoji recents across launches | on with the emoji keyboard | `@react-native-async-storage/async-storage` |
| Attachment menu tabs | on by default | `expo-media-library` / `expo-image-picker`, `expo-document-picker`, `expo-location` |
| File messages | `IMessage.file` | none; `expo-sharing` opens them in the share sheet |
| Rich markdown for AI replies | `messageTextProps={{ markdown: true }}` | none (built-in), `react-native-streamdown` upgrades it |
| Custom icons | `icons={{ send: … }}` | `react-native-svg` for the built-in Lucide glyphs |

## Streaming (AI) replies

```tsx
import { Chat, IMessage, useStreamingMessages } from '@kesha-antonov/react-native-chat'

const { messages, append, startStream, isStreaming, stop } = useStreamingMessages<IMessage>({ initialMessages })

const onSend = useCallback((newMessages: IMessage[] = []) => {
  append(newMessages[0])
  const stream = startStream({ user: { _id: 2, name: 'Assistant' } })

  runModel(newMessages[0].text, {
    signal: stream.signal,                // aborts when stop() is called
    onToken: token => stream.push(token), // batched, one render per frame
    onDone: () => stream.done(),
  })
}, [append, startStream])
```

Tokens are batched with `requestAnimationFrame`, and only the streaming bubble re-renders.
For a Stop button, swap the send button while streaming:
`renderSend={props => isStreaming ? <MyStopButton onPress={stop} /> : <Send {...props} />}`
(wrap it in `useCallback`). `messageTextProps={{ markdown: true }}` renders the reply as markdown.

## Emoji reactions

Reaction state is owned by the app, so it works with any backend. Passing `onReactionPress` turns
reactions on; it fires for both the picker and a pill tap, and `Chat.toggleReaction` applies it:

```tsx
<Chat
  reactions={{
    onReactionPress: (message, emoji) =>
      setMessages(prev => Chat.toggleReaction(prev, message._id, emoji, user._id)),
  }}
  {...props}
/>
```

A person can hold up to three reactions on a message (the oldest is replaced past that); pass
`{ maxPerUser: 1 }` as the fifth argument for one each. Pills show who reacted (`reactions.getUser`).

For a quick prototype, `const { chatProps } = useChatMessages({ initialMessages, user })` then
`<Chat {...chatProps} />` wires sending, reactions, editing and deleting to local state.

## Chat list

`ChatList` draws the list of chats (header with search, selection actions, archive folder,
swipe to archive, draggable pinned chats, unread counters, typing, drafts, loading placeholder).
Map your conversations to `ChatListItem` and pass a callback per action you support:

```tsx
<ChatList
  chats={chats}            // ChatListItem[]: { id, title, avatar?, kind?, lastMessage?, unreadCount?,
                           //   isPinned?, isMuted?, isArchived?, isOnline?, typingUsers?, typingAction?, draft? }
  user={me}
  onPressChat={chat => openChat(chat.id)}
  onArchiveChats={(selected, isArchived) => api.archive(selected, isArchived)}
  onReorderPinnedChats={ids => api.setPinnedOrder(ids)}
/>
```

Also `onPinChats`, `onMuteChats`, `onDeleteChats`, `onPressNewChat`, `onSearchChange`, and a
controlled archive folder (`isArchiveOpen` + `onArchiveOpenChange`). `TypingStatus` draws "Anna is
typing…" (or recording, sending media) for a header or row.

`useChatList(initialChats)` returns `{ chats, setChats, handlers, upsertChat, updateChat, receiveMessage,
markRead }` for local state: `<ChatList chats={list.chats} {...list.handlers} />`.

## Coming from react-native-gifted-chat

Same props, same `IMessage`. Swap the package and rename: `GiftedChat` → `Chat`,
`GiftedAvatar` → `ChatAvatar`, `GiftedChatContext` → `ChatContext`. Everything else -
`IMessage`, `User`, `useChatContext` - is unchanged. A codemod is in
[docs/MIGRATION.md](https://github.com/kesha-antonov/react-native-chat/blob/main/docs/MIGRATION.md).

## Common mistakes

- **Unstable render functions.** Rows share their props through a context kept stable between
  renders: inline handlers (`onPressMessage={() => …}`) and inline style/config objects are free,
  but a new render function (`renderBubble={props => …}`) re-renders every row - wrap render
  functions in `useCallback`.
- **Drawing a date in `renderMessage`.** The list draws the day separator around each row; a
  custom `renderMessage` that renders its own `<Day>` prints a date above every message.
- **Mutating messages in place.** Each row subscribes to its own message and notices a change
  when the message object is replaced, so always build new arrays and objects.
- **Drawing a neighbour's content.** `previousMessage` / `nextMessage` are kept current only for
  grouping (sender, day, time apart); a row does not re-render when a neighbour's text or status
  changes.
- **Setting `keyboardVerticalOffset` by hand.** Chat measures its own position on screen; a
  manual value replaces the measured one and usually leaves the toolbar floating. Pass one only
  to add deliberate extra space.
- **Nesting a second `GestureHandlerRootView`.** If the app already mounts one (directly or via
  a bottom-sheet library), set `enableGestureHandlerRootView={false}` - it cannot be
  auto-detected. An existing `KeyboardProvider` *is* detected and reused automatically.
- **Setting `FlatList` props.** The list is Legend List: `listProps` takes its props, and
  `inverted`, `windowSize` or `initialNumToRender` do nothing. `messagesContainerRef` is a
  `LegendListRef`.
- **Expecting `actionSheet()` to work out of the box.** The bundled
  `@expo/react-native-action-sheet` dependency was removed; prefer `messageActions`, or supply
  your own `actionSheet` implementation.
- **Forgetting the container.** `<Chat>` needs a parent with `flex: 1`.
